transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Ortiz (Redwood SE), Marcel Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Tom Alvarez (Zenvera Head Infra), Maya Chen (Zenvera Security Architect), Liam O'Connor (Procurement), Priya Rao (Eng Lead)

Intro / housekeeping (00:00)
Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we'll keep this as a security intake, our goal is to understand your constraints and then share the relevant artifacts. we'll try to be crisp, but feel free to interrupt.
Tom Alvarez: yeah thanks Alex, we have a hard requirement around PHI and EU residency so looking to see if Redwood can meet that with either Dedicated or Private.

Overview and high-level ask (03:14)
Maya Chen: quick context, zenvera processes clinical notes and manual lab results, so encryption at rest and in transit is must. we also need key separation — ideally BYOK where keys never leave our KMS.
Samira Ortiz: understood, we support both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK via customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSMs). for Private deployments we can run with a customer-controlled KMS endpoint inside the VPC.

SOC2 / ISO discussion (07:46)
Tom Alvarez: do you have SOC 2 Type II and any ISO 27001 attestations? if so how recent?
Alex Kim: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for our control plane and ISO 27001 in progress — our latest SOC report is for the last 12 months, we'll share the redacted PDF after this call. (murmur) also the dedicated control plane has additional isolation controls.
Maya Chen: can you confirm which controls map to data residency and key management? sometimes the wording in reports is high level.
Alex Kim: good point, Samira will map the relevant controls to your requirements and include the control IDs. expect that in the packages we send.

KMS / encryption deep dive (15:02)
Samira Ortiz: quick note on the implementation — for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed master keys; BYOK is available for customers on Dedicated/Private. for BYOK we support rotating keys on your schedule, and we never persist the unwrapped key outside the KMS.
Priya Rao: what about performance impacts, if keys are in a remote HSM? our latency budget for inference is tight.
Samira Ortiz: yes there's a small upfront overhead for initial model loading when using customer KMS due to key unwraps, but during token generation we cache the unwrapped material in the runtime's KV cache — that's standard, so steady-state doesn't add per-token KMS calls. however if you want vault-less operation we can add a local wrapping key for Dedicated for the session with controls. (slight pause) we'll document CPU/latency delta from our benchmarks.

SSO / RBAC / provisioning (21:10)
Maya Chen: we use Okta for SSO and need SAML + SCIM user provisioning. RBAC needs to map to our teams — ability to limit model deployment and see audit logs per-project.
Alex Kim: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC is role-based with custom roles available at the enterprise tier. Admins can constrain model access, create route-level policies, and require MFA. we'll share the RBAC model doc and an example SCIM manifest.
Maya Chen: can RBAC be integrated with existing groups provisioned from Okta?
Samira Ortiz: yes, groups map into Redwood roles; we support SCIM group sync so that you can manage access from Okta. some customers push it further with just-in-time role elevation but that requires an extra connector.

Audit logs and retention (29:38)
Tom Alvarez: our security policy requires 365+ days of immutable logs for access and admin actions, and the ability to export logs to our ELK stack. how do your logs look?
Alex Kim: we retain audit logs in the control plane for configurable windows; default for enterprise is 1 year. we provide structured JSON logs with fields for user, route/model, tokens_consumed, request_id, and KV cache hits. exports can be pushed to S3, Cloud Storage, or streamed via a SIEM connector.
Maya Chen: are logs tamper-evident? do you support write-once storage?
Marcel Nguyen: we can support WORM for archived buckets and deliver signed manifests for tamper evidence; we also provide cryptographic checksums on log bundles.

Data residency and deletion (35:02)
Priya Rao: EU residency — can we ensure inference requests for EU customers stay in eu-west region and that nothing crosses the atlantic?
Samira Ortiz: yes, routing policies can pin requests by geo, org, or model. for Private deployments we operate entirely inside your VPC so nothing leaves. for Hosted we have region pins and we can sign an addendum for guaranteed regional routing within our SLA.
Liam O'Connor: retention — do you keep prompts or embeddings by default? what are delete semantics?
Alex Kim: by default, Hosted does not retain request payloads beyond short-term logs for debugging, but customers can opt into longer storage. for enterprise we support no-retention mode, and for Dedicated/Private you can disable retention entirely. we'll include exact API flags and deletion endpoints.

Tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (41:28)
Tom Alvarez: we're leaning toward Dedicated but need clarity on cost delta vs Hosted and operations overhead. also if we pick Dedicated, can we have private KMS and restrict egress?
Samira Ortiz: Dedicated is the middle ground — predictable capacity and ability to BYOK with private KMS; Private gives full control (VPC, air-gapped if needed) but is the most ops-heavy. Hosted is easiest but requires trust and certain legal addenda for PHI. We'll provide a sheet with estimated run rate and delta for K80 vs A100 equivalent configs.

Procurement / timeline (48:15)
Liam O'Connor: our procurement window is end of month, we need a proposal and rough SOW. can you provide a standard PO template?
Alex Kim: yes, we'll attach Redwood's standard enterprise SOW and a PO template. once procurement confirms, we can schedule the POC.

Wrap and next steps (53:02)
Alex Kim: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO PDFs, a KMS integration diagram, RBAC/SCIM examples, logs export doc, and a pricing delta sheet. Samira will own the KMS doc, I'll drop the SOC pack, Marcel will send the log export checklist. propose a 2-hr POC next Tuesday to run benchmarks and validate latency with your Okta staging.
Tom Alvarez: sounds good, thanks. Maya: thanks, that clarifies a lot.

Closing (57:30)
Alex Kim: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts. thanks everyone.
